messages:
bri (product): Heads-up — planning thread for org-scoped API keys + migration constraints. Customer asks + launch criteria. Keeping this short: need design decisions on backcompat, rotation semantics, admin UX, and SDK migration path.

devin (eng-api): quick notes:
- two token types: `org_....` and `proj_....` (proposal).
- router will accept both for a transition period. auth flow: header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` plus optional `X-Project-Id` for org keys to act on a specific project.
- backcompat: existing keys -> treated as `proj_` tokens bound to legacy default project mapping.

olga (security): important: rotation semantics must be explicit. if an org key rotates, we should NOT auto-invalidate project-level keys unless customer requests. Otherwise huge blast radius. Audit events needed: `key.create`, `key.rotate`, `key.revoke`, `key.exchange`. We also need KMS/HSM markers in metadata.

maya (platform): DB work: add `scope` enum on `api_keys` (org|project), `org_id` nullable, `project_id` nullable. Migration plan: backfill legacy keys as `project` scoped with `project_id = legacy_default_project`. This allows routing to continue. We'll need a short window where router accepts both header shapes.

bryan (cs): customer asks we've surfaced: enterprise customers want
- ability to rotate org keys without downtime for services that use project keys
- admin UI for issuing project-scoped keys under an org, with HMAC display only once
- migration tool to map old keys to projects or bulk-create new project keys and exchange tokens.

devin (eng-api): implementation details:
```
# token handling pseudocode
if token.startswith("org_"):
  claims = verify_org_token(token)
  project = request.header.get('X-Project-Id') or claims.get('default_project')
else:
  claims = verify_project_token(token)
  project = claims.project_id
```
Edge-case: if org token used without X-Project-Id and no default, reject with 400 and guidance link.

olga (security): rotation policy options:
- soft-rotate (create new token, old remains valid for 24h) -> lower customer pain, harder revocation
- hard-rotate (new token active immediately, old revokes) -> stronger security, needs migration tooling
Recommend default: soft-rotate with ability to hard-revoke on demand. Document recommended TTLs and rotation cadence.

maya (platform): rollout plan (high level):
1) DB + API boolean feature flag (internal)
2) router accepts org/proj tokens (canary to 5% infra)
3) offer opt-in migration API + SDK helper to exchange old key -> project key
4) open beta with enterprise customers only (30 days)
5) full launch + admin UI + audit streaming

bryan (cs): launch criteria we need to sign off on from GTM/CS:
- migration CLI + SDK helpers available
- docs and sample scripts
- e2e test matrix (rotation, exchange, RBAC) green
- audit logs flowing to customer SIEM (via syslog/HTTP)
- at least 2 enterprise customers onboarded in beta

devin (eng-api): integrations: SDK change is tiny — auto-detect `org_` prefix and accept an optional `project` param on client constructors. We'll include a deprecation warning when legacy tokens used.

olga (security): add these checks to threat model:
- org token leakage -> enumerate all projects; ensure read-only option for org tokens is available (scoped by permissions).
- require `org_admin` role to create org-scoped keys in UI/API.

infra-bot: deployment note: canary deploy planned 2025-11-12T16:00Z -> will create feature-flag gate `org_keys_v1`. Monitor: `auth.failure.rate`, `key.exchange.errors`, and `audit.events.rate`.

bri (product): open decisions we need to close this sprint:
- default rotation mode (olga suggested soft-rotate)
- whether org tokens can be created with limited scopes (yes -> need permission model)
- migration UX: bulk exchange tool vs automatic mapping (CS prefers exchange tool + manual mapping).

devin (eng-api): +1 to exchange tool. automatic mapping is risky (wrong project mapping). Exchange flow: customer uploads CSV of legacy keys -> we create project keys and return map, with option to revoke legacy keys.

olga (security): final ask: plan for emergency revocation path (single API call to revoke all keys for an org) + papertrail entries for legal/compliance.

maya (platform): I'll draft RFC with DB schema, migration steps, and rollout gating. Will include sample audit event shapes.

bri (product): thanks. action items: @maya draft RFC by EOD Wed, @devin prototype SDK helper, @olga write rotation policy doc, @bryan schedule 1:1 with pilot customers. I'll collate launch criteria for exec review. :thumbsup:

olga (security): ack :lock:

devin (eng-api): will start a small PR for header parsing and token detection today.

bryan (cs): I'll prepare a short customer comms template for migration (FAQ + timeline).

infra-bot: noted. Canary window scheduled. Logs forwarded to #eng-sre.

bri (product): we'll reconvene Friday to review RFC + pilot signups. If anyone has objections to the soft-rotate default, reply here.
